ai.title: Lazy-load project files on demand
ai.summary: Project files are now loaded lazily via requestFiles instead of eagerly in updateFileContext. The ProjectFileContextSchema allows null values for missing files, and the system prompt instructs the agent to explicitly request files not in the context before modification. Token counting logic handles null content by returning 0.

eli5.text: Starting today, the coding assistant no longer loads every project file into memory the moment you open a project. Instead, it waits and loads a file only when you specifically ask it to read or edit that file. When you request a file that isn't already open, the assistant will explicitly fetch it before making changes, and if a requested file doesn't exist, it will be noted as missing rather than causing an error. This means the assistant will feel more responsive when working in large projects, and you may see files appear or disappear from context as you interact with them rather than all at once. This change is live today.

ai.title: Propagate fingerprint ID to Helicone user ID for backend requests
ai.summary: Backend LLM calls now include a Helicone-User-Id header derived from the client's fingerprint ID. The fingerprint ID is threaded through WebSocket actions, main prompt handlers, and API clients in claude.ts and openai-api.ts. This change affects shared types in common/src/actions.ts and the npm client in npm-app/src/client.ts. A minor system prompt update clarifies comment generation rules.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to generate code, each of your requests now carries a tracking tag (your fingerprint ID) that flows through the backend into the analytics layer as your Helicone user ID. This means every backend LLM call, whether it goes to Claude or OpenAI, is attributed to you, so your usage can be monitored for rate limits and security policies. The tag is passed through the WebSocket connection, the main prompt handler, and the file-request pipeline, and you would notice it as consistently attributed requests in the Helicone dashboard rather than anonymous traffic. It is live today for all requests that include a fingerprint ID.

ai.title: Pass userId to patch generation pipeline
ai.summary: Backend patch generation functions now accept and propagate a userId parameter. This threads the user identifier through generatePatch, processFileBlock, and downstream prompt generators like generateDiffBlocks and expandNewContent. The change ensures internal API calls for diff and patch generation are attributed to the correct user context. No breaking changes to external interfaces; internal refactoring only.

eli5.text: When the assistant creates code changes for your request, each change is now tagged with your account ID so it can be tracked back to you in the backend. This is an internal housekeeping update that does not change what you see or do, but helps the team attribute generated diffs and patches correctly. If you never look at logs, you will notice nothing, but the system now reliably credits each generated change to the right user.

ai.title: Add Helicone rate limit policy to Claude and OpenAI API calls
ai.summary: Added `Helicone-RateLimit-Policy` header to `promptClaudeStream`, `promptClaude`, and `getOpenAI` default headers. Policy string `2000;w=86400;u=cents;s=user` defined in new `backend/src/constants.ts`. Scope limited to backend API clients.

eli5.text: When the system talks to the Claude and OpenAI assistants behind the scenes, it now quietly tells them to pace themselves: roughly 2,000 paid calls per user per day, with usage tallied in cents, and any overages throttled back. This rate limit lives in a small shared settings file that only the backend server-side code reads, so everyday users won't notice anything different unless they hit those usage caps. It's live today for any backend requests routed through the updated API connections.

ai.title: Add userId argument to generateExpandedFileWithDiffBlocks in tests
ai.summary: Added missing 'userId' argument to generateExpandedFileWithDiffBlocks call in diff-prompt.test.ts. Fixes type error.

eli5.text: The assistant now passes along a user identifier when running its automated test checks, fixing a behind-the-scenes type error in the testing script. This is internal housekeeping only and does not change any behavior you would see, since the test suite is not something end users interact with directly. It is live today as part of the test files, but nothing a reader of this change would notice has changed in the product itself.

ai.title: Enable Helicone LLM Security on Claude and OpenAI clients
ai.summary: Added 'Helicone-LLM-Security-Enabled': 'true' header to Helicone proxy requests in backend/src/claude.ts and backend/src/openai-api.ts. This activates Helicone's LLM security layer for both Claude and OpenAI API streams. Scope covers backend service clients only; no frontend or config changes.

eli5.text: This is a behind-the-scenes change that turns on security monitoring for internal requests sent to Claude and OpenAI models. Only the backend systems that route requests through Helicone are affected; the web app and configuration files were not modified. If you looked now, you'd see the security layer running, but since it's an internal safeguard, there is no visible feature for end users yet.

eli5.text: An internal tool the team relies on quietly ticked its version number up by one small step, and nothing else changed about how it behaves. You wouldn't notice anything different while using the assistant because no features, buttons, or workflows were added or adjusted. This kind of change is just routine housekeeping to keep the behind-the-scenes tooling tidy and running smoothly, not an update you'd see or feel.

ai.title: Scrape URLs from user input
ai.summary: Client.ts now parses URLs from the last user message and appends scraped content blocks, mirroring existing knowledge.md handling. Logic extracted to web-scraper.ts getScrapedContentBlocks. System prompt reordered to prioritize file context requests over code review.

eli5.text: Starting today, when you paste a web link into Manicode, the assistant will automatically fetch the page content and include it in its analysis, rather than ignoring the link. This works for any URL you add in your message; the assistant now reads the page behind the link just like it reads files you attach, and then reasons over that content alongside your code. If you previously saw the assistant skip over links and ask you to paste their text manually, that should no longer happen for new conversations.

eli5.text: Today the AI coding assistant quietly bumped its internal version number from 1.0.38 to 1.0.39 with no new capabilities or fixes for end users. You won't see any difference in menus, speed, or features because this release only adjusts a behind-the-scenes label that programmers and package managers use to track updates. It's already live as part of routine release housekeeping, so the version shown in developer tools, logs, or command-line prompts will now read 1.0.39 instead of 1.0.38.

ai.title: Skip redundant file check instructions in system prompt after initial
ai.summary: System prompt generation now accepts a checkFiles boolean to conditionally exclude the instruction to request missing files. This prevents the agent from re-evaluating file context immediately after updateFileContext has already populated it during the initial prompt setup. Logic resides in backend/src/main-prompt.ts and backend/src/system-prompt.ts, adjusting the general case instructions based on the shouldCheckFiles flag.

eli5.text: When you start a new conversation with the system, it now skips a step where it would normally re-scan your project files for missing context, since that scan already happened during setup. The assistant will only ask you to point it at additional files if it genuinely hasn't looked at your project yet, rather than asking every time it generates a reply. You won't notice a difference in the assistant's output, but it will avoid a redundant instruction telling it to check files it already has in context. This is a behind-the-scenes adjustment that trims a repeated prompt instruction and is live today.

ai.title: Add delete-comment mock data and patch test
ai.summary: Added `delete-comment` mock files (`expected.ts`, `new.ts`, `old.ts`) under `backend/src/__tests__/__mock-data__/`. Registered a new test case 'should remove try catch in delete comment' in `generate-patch.test.ts`. The mocks demonstrate the transition from error-wrapped deletion logic to direct execution.

eli5.text: When you delete a comment, the system used to wrap every deletion in a safety net that caught errors, printed a message, and rethrew a generic failure. That safety net has been taken out, so the deletion now runs directly without the extra error handling. If you were watching the logs, you would no longer see the extra error messages or the fallback logic when something goes wrong during a deletion; the operation either succeeds or fails without the surrounding try-catch block. This is internal housekeeping that only affects the backend code path for deleting comments, and it is already live in the system today.

ai.title: Expansion edits use gpt-4o
ai.summary: generate-diffs-via-expansion.ts swaps gpt-4o-mini for gpt-4o-2024-08-06 in the expansion edit pipeline. gpt-4o matches mini's speed while delivering higher quality edits. Change scoped to backend diff generation logic.

eli5.text: The system that rewrites text edits now asks a more capable version of the assistant to do the work. Instead of using the quick-and-small helper, edits are generated by the full version, which catches more subtle mistakes yet still works just as fast. You won't see a button change, but edits that fix slightly trickier formatting or wording issues now succeed where the smaller helper sometimes missed them. The change is live today in the backend that powers those text rewrites.

ai.title: gpt-4o-2024-08-06 replaces gpt-4o-mini for file requests
ai.summary: backend/src/request-files-prompt.ts switches the comprehensive file request model from 'gpt-4o-mini' to 'gpt-4o-2024-08-06'. The 'Key' model request path using models.sonnet is commented out, leaving only the comprehensive path active. getRelevantFiles routing logic updated to check model.startsWith('gpt') instead of strict equality. Scope limited to backend request files prompt logic.

eli5.text: When the system needs to find the right files to work with, it now uses a newer, faster version of the assistant behind the scenes instead of the older, slower one it used before. You won't see a button to flip, but the file-picking step that powers your tasks should feel a bit quicker and more accurate as a result. The change is already live, so any request that pulls in relevant files is using the upgraded version now.

ai.title: Switch diff generation to gpt-4o
ai.summary: Backend diff generation now uses `promptOpenAIWithContinuation` with `gpt-4o-2024-08-06` instead of `promptClaudeWithContinuation`. Added `promptOpenAIWithContinuation` in `backend/src/openai-api.ts` to handle streaming, stop markers, and automatic continuation logic. Updated `backend/src/generate-diffs-prompt.ts` to import the new helper and adjust prompt instructions for unique block matching.

eli5.text: You may notice that the assistant now produces code diffs using a different model (gpt-4o) instead of the previous one (Claude), which can result in slightly different formatting and matching behavior when locating and replacing code segments. Behind the scenes, the system switched the diff generation engine it uses, added new helper logic to handle how responses are streamed and stopped, and adjusted the instructions given to the model so it finds uniquely matching code blocks rather than just any matching block. This is a backend-only change and does not affect any settings or controls you interact with directly.
